cards.title: Us Against the Problem
cards.intent: Remain visible throughout dialogue to keep both partners united against the cycle rather than litigating blame.

steps: We are two partners sitting on the same side of the table tackling a shared cycle together—not adversaries litigating blame.
THE SHARED COMMONS: Neither partner owns these cards. We both draw from the same shared palette of moves.
CONNECTION OVER COMPLIANCE: Never use the cards to 'catch' your partner breaking a rule. If it feels punitive, reset.
TWO REALITIES STAND TOGETHER: Acknowledging your partner's pain never erases your own experience or good intentions.
PAUSING IS A COMMITMENT: Anyone can pause at any time. Pausing means we promise to return when our nervous systems settle.

guardrails: No quoting rules as accusations ('You violated Rule 2!').
No treating the conversation as a court case with a winner & loser.
No talking when heart rates exceed ~100 BPM.

cards.title: Two Realities Can Stand Together
cards.intent: Remind both partners that validating emotional pain does not require conceding fault or erasing the other's perspective.

steps: Validating your partner’s emotional reality does NOT mean conceding fault, admitting defeat, or rewriting history.
Two people can experience the exact same 30 seconds completely differently and both be speaking the emotional truth.
Acknowledging hurt is not admitting you are a bad partner.
Your parked stickies will not be forgotten. First we make room for one experience, then we cross the bridge to the other.

guardrails: No litigating a single, objective 'historical court transcript.'
No withholding empathy out of fear it will be used against you.
No jumping into your side before your partner feels registered.

cards.title: The Invitation: Propose a Talk & Agree on Time
cards.intent: Check availability and set a firm time boundary so neither partner feels ambushed, cornered, or trapped in an endless marathon.

steps: Name a single, specific topic (no kitchen-sinking).
Propose a firm time cap (15–20 minutes maximum).
You keep the floor once agreed—place your content card next!
Check your capacity honestly: accept now, adjust time, or raincheck.
You do NOT need to play a card just to say yes.

guardrails: No ambushing while walking out the door or right before sleep.
No piling multiple unresolved complaints into one invitation.
No marathon talks with unspecified end times.

verbal_formulas.script: I’d love to talk through [single topic] so we can get on the same page. Do you have 20 minutes right now?
Yes, I have capacity now. / I'm running on empty right now; can we sit down at 7:00 PM after dinner? (Play B-04)

cards.title: Check-In on Bandwidth & Capacity
cards.intent: Prevent starting a deep conversation when either nervous system is operating on empty battery.

steps: State your current emotional and physical battery level (1–10).
Name any background drains (fatigue, hunger, work overload).
Share your honest battery level without matching out of guilt.
If either partner is below 4/10, downscale the talk or reschedule.

guardrails: No faking a 9/10 when depleted just to get it over with.
No guilt-tripping a partner for being at low battery.
No opening heavy relational topics if either partner is under 4/10.

verbal_formulas.script: On a scale of 1–10, my battery is around a [X]. I'm also carrying [work stress / headache / fatigue].
I'm sitting at a [Y]. Given where we're at, let's keep this focused / let's grab food first / let's talk tomorrow.

cards.title: Wrap Up, Appreciate & Ground
cards.intent: Step out of the conversation with mutual warmth and clear the air so residual tension does not spill into the rest of the day.

steps: Name one specific thing your partner did well during the talk.
Clear and recycle used stickies from the table mat.
Return a specific appreciation for how your partner showed up.
Join in physical contact (handhold or grounding hug) to land.

guardrails: No slipping in 'one last grievance' on the way out the door.
No passive-aggressive lingering or cold treatment after wrapping up.
No reopening the issue once cards are gathered.

verbal_formulas.script: Thank you for [not getting defensive / listening so patiently when I was clumsy]. That really helped me stay grounded.
Thank you for bringing this up with care. We are good, and I love you.

cards.title: Schedule a Conscious Raincheck
cards.intent: Postpone dialogue safely when exhausted or flooded without letting it deteriorate into avoidant stonewalling.

steps: Own the constraint cleanly (exhaustion, sensory overload, timing).
Offer a specific, non-negotiable return time within 24 hours.
Accept the deferral without punitive commentary.
Write your topic on a sticky note and park it under this card.

guardrails: No saying 'we'll talk later' without a concrete calendar time.
No using rainchecks as an escape hatch to avoid the subject forever.
No guilt-tripping your partner for needing to postpone.

verbal_formulas.script: I really care about this, but my head is spinning / I am running on empty. Can we sit down tomorrow morning at 9:30 AM?
Yes. I will write this down and park it. We will pick it up tomorrow at 9:30 AM.

cards.title: Share Hurt / Impact
cards.intent: Express the emotional sting of an event cleanly without turning it into a courtroom prosecution of your partner's character.

steps: Stick strictly to neutral, camera-observable facts (what happened).
Name your internal story and the primary vulnerable emotion.
Speak only about your internal experience, not their intent.
Absorb the emotional impact without interrupting.
If defensive rebuttals surge, write a sticky note and park it!

guardrails: No 'You make me feel...' statements or character assassinations.
No absolute generalizations ('You always...', 'You never...').
No unsolicited counter-explanations from the receiver.

verbal_formulas.script: When [specific factual event happened], the story I made up was [X], and what I felt underneath was [hurt / alone / scared].
I hear that that stung. Let me make sure I'm taking that in before I say anything else. (Play P-01 or P-02)

cards.title: Bid for Reassurance
cards.intent: Voice relationship anxiety or tender insecurity when no acute fight has happened, asking for warmth and grounding.

steps: Own the insecurity as internal rather than blaming your partner.
Clearly ask for relational reassurance and warmth.
Offer immediate, unreserved warmth and physical contact.
Resist debating whether the insecurity is 'rational.'

guardrails: No logical dismissals ('Why ask that? Of course we're fine, silly').
No treating vulnerability as high-maintenance or needy.
No passive-aggressive fishing for compliments.

verbal_formulas.script: You haven't done anything wrong. My own insecurity is high today, and I just need to hear that we are okay and you love me.
We are completely good. I love you, and I am right here with you. (Offer hug or handhold)

cards.title: Name the Attachment Fear / Raw Wound
cards.intent: Drop beneath surface irritation to expose the primal relational vulnerability fueling your reaction.

steps: Look beneath anger, snapping, or withdrawal.
Name the deeper fear: being unworthy, unloved, alone, or a burden.
Treat this as sacred ground—soften your voice, posture, and facial expression immediately.
Hold space for the fear without arguing facts.

guardrails: No debating whether they 'should' have that attachment fear.
No weaponizing past wounds ('You're just acting like your dad').
No hiding vulnerability behind sarcastic humor.

verbal_formulas.script: Underneath my snap, what I was really feeling was: [I don't matter to you / I'm failing you / I'm all alone].
Thank you for showing me that soft spot. It hurts to hear you felt that, and I want you to feel safe with me.

cards.title: Own My Part Early
cards.intent: Disarm escalation at the outset by voluntarily naming your own unhelpful behavior before being called out.

steps: Name your specific action or tone with clean accountability.
Keep it free of excuses or conditional clauses.
Receive the ownership with clean gratitude.
Do not use it as leverage or a victory lap.

guardrails: No conditional apologies ('I was short, BUT only because you...').
No self-pitying theatrics ('I guess I'm just the worst partner').
No gloating ('Finally you admit you were wrong!').

verbal_formulas.script: Looking back at earlier, I see where I contributed: I was short with you / I rolled my eyes / I checked out. That wasn't fair.
Thank you for acknowledging that unprompted. That really helps my nervous system relax.

cards.title: Paraphrase & Mirror
cards.intent: Prove you are absorbing your partner's actual words rather than rehearsing your rebuttal in your head.

steps: Echo back what you heard using their core words.
Check for accuracy before offering any interpretation.
Listen to hear if your meaning landed.
Confirm with a gentle nod or clarify the missing nuance cleanly.

guardrails: No sarcastic parroting or exaggerated tone.
No inserting your own editorial spin into the summary.
No moving on until the speaker feels accurately mirrored.

verbal_formulas.script: What I hear you saying is that when [X] happened, you felt [Y] and it left you feeling [Z]. Did I capture that accurately?
Yes, exactly. / You got most of it, but the part that hurt deepest was actually [nuance].

cards.title: Validate Emotional Logic
cards.intent: Confirm that your partner's emotional response makes rational sense given their perspective and what they experienced.

steps: Connect their feeling to what they perceived or their past history.
Affirm the emotional validity of their reaction completely.
Notice how your body registers the validation.
Let the comfort in without immediately escalating with new points.

guardrails: No poisonous 'BUT...' clauses ('I get why you felt that, BUT...').
No debating whether their feelings are logically 'justified.'
No treating validation as a legal admission of guilt.

verbal_formulas.script: Given that you saw [X] and thought [Y], it makes complete sense that you felt hurt / alone / shut down.
Thank you for seeing that. That makes a big difference to hear out loud.

cards.title: Curious Check-In / Tender Question
cards.intent: Lean in with genuine warmth to explore what is happening beneath the surface without asking interrogating questions.

steps: Ask an open-ended, non-leading emotional question.
Listen purely to understand, not to gather evidence for a defense.
Speak to your interior world; trust the open door.
Focus on what was hardest for you in that moment.

guardrails: No trap questions ('Don't you think you overreacted?').
No cross-examining factual timelines or inconsistencies.
No interrupting their answer to correct their memory.

verbal_formulas.script: I notice distance between us / some tension in the air. What's on your heart? What was the hardest part of that for you?
What felt hardest was feeling like I wasn't being taken seriously when I brought up [Topic].

cards.title: Name the Underlying Need
cards.intent: Help translate anger or frustration into the universal human relational need sitting underneath.

steps: Offer a gentle, tentative guess about their core emotional need.
Hold your guess lightly without insisting you are right.
Check inside: does that hit the mark, or is the need different?
Name what would help you feel safe, valued, or connected.

guardrails: No diagnosing or dictating what they 'should' need.
No shaming them for having basic attachment needs.
No jumping directly into problem-solving until the need is clear.

verbal_formulas.script: It sounds like in that moment, what you really needed was to feel prioritized / supported / held. Is that what was missing?
Yes, exactly. I just needed to know you were in my corner.

cards.title: Context & My Reality
cards.intent: Share missing timeline details or internal pressures without wiping out your partner's emotional experience.

steps: Re-affirm your partner's hurt first.
Offer your internal state as information, never justification.
Pull in any parked sticky notes from Quadrant 1 on the mat.
Receive the context as missing pieces of the puzzle.
Remember that hearing their context doesn't cancel your hurt.

guardrails: No using context to erase impact ('I had a bad day, so let it go').
No playing before your partner's feelings have been validated.
No competing over who had a harder day or more stress.

verbal_formulas.script: Now that I've heard your hurt, can I share what was happening on my end? I was dealing with [overload / work stress], which is what led to [action].
I can hear that you were overloaded. It helps me see the whole picture, even though it still hurt.

cards.title: Intention vs. Impact Reconciliation
cards.intent: Own the painful gap between what you meant to do and what your partner actually experienced.

steps: Clarify the positive or neutral goal you were pursuing.
Unequivocally apologize for the unintended hurt that landed.
Make space for the reality of their positive/neutral intent.
Hold both: they didn't mean to wound you, AND you were wounded.

guardrails: No 'That's not what I meant, so you shouldn't feel hurt.'
No defending clumsy behavior purely behind good intentions.
No minimizing the impact as illogical or unreasonable.

verbal_formulas.script: My intention was [helpful / peaceful X]. However, I see clearly that the impact on you was [hurt / loneliness Y]. I am so sorry that my actions produced that outcome.
I appreciate knowing you didn't mean to hurt me. That helps me release the story that you were trying to attack me.

cards.title: Share My Parallel Trigger
cards.intent: Share what historical wound or tender spot was activated in you so both partners can see why the mutual collision occurred.

steps: Name the old wound or raw nerve touched during the interaction.
Frame your reaction as self-protection, not malicious retaliation.
Recognize that both nervous systems were triggered simultaneously.
Hold their trigger with equal care and respect.

guardrails: No comparing triggers ('My trigger was worse than yours').
No using your past trigger as a permanent excuse for poor behavior.
No mocking or minimizing their historical sensitivities.

verbal_formulas.script: When [X] happened, it hit an old wound for me: I felt [criticized / micromanaged / dismissed], which triggered my walls.
I see how that poked your raw spot. I can understand why your defenses went up so quickly.

cards.title: Map Our Shared Cycle (The Bridge)
cards.intent: Reframe the fight from 'You vs. Me' to 'Us vs. The Cycle.'

steps: Trace the mutual feedback loop step by step.
Externalize the cycle as the common enemy catching both of you.
Warmly invite the second partner's experience into focus.

guardrails: No assigning origin blame ('You started the loop!').
No rigid psychological labeling ('You're the avoider/pursuer').
No litigating past historical instances of the cycle.

verbal_formulas.script: When [Trigger] happens, I tend to [Reaction A], which makes you feel [Feeling B], so you react by [Reaction B], which pulls me right back into [Reaction A].
That’s the exact loop. We both get trapped in it. Now that we see it, can I share what happened on my side?

cards.title: I Feel Met / Your Turn to Share
cards.intent: A voluntary, organic completion move by the first speaker to step back, thank their partner, and open the floor to their experience.

steps: Affirm that your nervous system feels settled and heard.
Warmly invite your partner's internal experience into the light.
Unpark your sticky notes from the table mat.
Speak from your own experience, not as an attack on what was said.

guardrails: No closing the track if unresolved hurt is still actively burning.
No treating the second turn as a cross-examination rebuttal.
No rushing your partner when they step forward to share.

verbal_formulas.script: Thank you for listening so carefully. I feel registered on my piece. I want to clear the floor for you—what was this like for you?
Thank you. What was coming up for me while listening was [X], and I’d like to share my piece now. (Play Teal or Amber)

cards.title: Small Behavioral Experiment
cards.intent: Commit to a tangible, bite-sized behavioral test for the coming week instead of making sweeping, unrealistic promises.

steps: Pick ONE concrete, observable action to test for the next 7 days.
Agree on a specific check-in time to review how it felt.

guardrails: No sweeping, impossible promises ('I will never get upset again').
No one-sided agreements where only one partner does all the adapting.
No treating a minor slip-up during the week as a total failure.

verbal_formulas.script: Next time [Trigger] occurs, what if we try [Micro-Action] for 7 days and see if it takes the edge off?
I like that. Let's test it for one week and review on Sunday after breakfast. (Write on sticky note)

cards.title: Needs Co-Design
cards.intent: Treat differing relational needs as an optimization puzzle to solve together rather than an irreconcilable incompatibility.

steps: Name both needs side by side without ranking one above the other.
Brainstorm setups where both needs are respected at least 80%.

guardrails: No treating your need as 'normal' and your partner's need as 'crazy.'
No zero-sum bargaining ('I won't do X unless you do Y').
No agreeing to an arrangement that builds hidden resentment.

verbal_formulas.script: My core need in this is [Need A: e.g. prompt check-ins].
My core need in this is [Need B: e.g. quiet decompression time]. How do we build a setup that honors both of those?

cards.title: Flooding Time-Out (20-Minute Reset)
cards.intent: Halt dialogue when heart rates exceed ~100 BPM and the prefrontal cortex goes offline, preventing biological escalation.

steps: Signal biological overload (tight chest, racing pulse, spinning).
Set a timer for 20 minutes and state a mandatory return time.
Soothe your nervous system (walk, cold water, breathing).
Honor the break instantly—no parting words or trailing pursuit.
Use the time to regulate, not rehearse counter-arguments.

guardrails: No parting jabs or zingers on the way out of the room.
No weaponizing breaks to stonewall or avoid returning.
No ruminating or building prosecution files while on break.

verbal_formulas.script: My nervous system is flooded and I cannot listen well. I need a 20-minute break. I will be back at [exact time].
I hear you. Let's take the 20 minutes. I will see you at [exact time].

cards.title: Process Weaponization / Grace Reset
cards.intent: Stop either partner from using the card framework as a weapon or acting like a rigid process referee.

steps: Call out process policing gently without shaming.
Ask for a clean reset of tone and posture.
Exhale, laugh, or drop defensiveness immediately.
Release the preceding 3 minutes from active debate.
Take three synchronized deep breaths together.

guardrails: No saying 'You played that card wrong!' or 'You broke Rule 3!'
No penalizing each other for needing a reset.
No carrying pre-reset arguments into the renewed space.

verbal_formulas.script: We're starting to litigate the rules rather than connect. Let's call a Grace Reset, take three breaths, and start fresh.
You're right. I was getting into process-cop mode. Let's take three breaths together.

cards.title: 60-Second Grounding Hug
cards.intent: Use mammalian nervous system co-regulation to drain fight-or-flight adrenaline without needing spoken words.

steps: Gently ask permission for physical contact.
Hold silently for a full 60 seconds with steady, deep exhalations.
Accept, modify, or decline touch freely without guilt.
If accepted, drop physical tension in jaw, neck, and shoulders.

guardrails: No speaking, explaining, or sighing sarcastically during the hug.
No taking touch refusal as personal rejection when overstimulated.
No sexualizing grounding contact during conflict.

verbal_formulas.script: Can we pause the words and do a 60-second hug just to ground our nervous systems?
Yes, please. / I'm too overstimulated for a full hug; can we just hold hands for a minute?
